The irony is that there currently isn't any such thing as a "Nordic alcohol culture" because alcohol (and most other "luxury" goods) are heavily taxed to pay for the welfare state.

I fondly remember the absolute look of disbelief I saw on the faces of two Swedish exchange students when they saw that a bottle of rum can cost as little as five euros over here.

I don't know if you can call it "Nordic alcohol culture" but there definitively are differences between alcohol cultures around the world.

There is a "climate line" that runs laterally through Europe, that determines what crops are most easily grown. The areas that can more easily grow beer- och wine producing crops have a different alcohol culture compared to the northern parts where it's easiest to grow strong alcohol producing crops (vodka).

  • In the southern parts, a majority of the alcohol consumed is generally consumed together with meals, as a natural part of the meal (like rice in east asian countries). The purpose of the alcohol intake is not to get drunk.

  • In northern parts, a majority of the alcohol consumed is generally consumed at parties / clubs etc. In this case, the main purpose of alcohol intake is often to get drunk.

The former generally leads to more health problems (lots of beer = generally bad for you) whilst the latter generally leads to more violence problems (lots of drunks in same place = lots of rowdyness).
